title: Counting objects
content: Count each object once. Say the number names in order. The last number said tells how many objects there are.

title: Joining groups
content: Addition joins quantities. For 2 + 3, start with 2 and count on three steps: 3, 4, 5. Therefore 2 + 3 = 5.

title: Taking away
content: Subtraction can show what remains. If you have 7 counters and remove 2, count the 5 counters left. Therefore 7 - 2 = 5.

title: Equal groups
content: Multiplication describes equal groups. Three groups of 4 contain 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 objects, so 3 x 4 = 12.

title: Sharing equally
content: Division shares or groups equally. Sharing 12 objects among 3 learners gives 4 objects to each learner, so 12 / 3 = 4.

title: Equal parts
content: A fraction describes equal parts. If a shape is divided into 4 equal parts and 1 part is shaded, the shaded fraction is 1/4.

title: Tenths and hundredths
content: The first digit after the decimal point represents tenths. The second represents hundredths. Thus 0.25 means 2 tenths and 5 hundredths.

title: Parts out of one hundred
content: Percent means out of 100. To find 25% of 40, calculate 25/100 x 40 = 10.

title: Comparing quantities
content: A ratio compares quantities in the same order. If there are 2 red beads and 3 blue beads, the ratio of red to blue is 2:3.

title: Keeping equations balanced
content: An equation stays balanced when the same operation is performed on both sides. For x + 4 = 9, subtract 4 from both sides to get x = 5.
